matches.rationale: The ground truth concerns an overstatement in the Abstract of a clear linear relationship and saturating variability, while the relevant finding (pred_id 1) claims the Abstract understates the correlation. No finding captures this specific overstatement issue.
The ground truth describes a fabricated citation 'Grant, 2025'. None of the predicted findings refer to any fabricated reference or citation error.
The ground truth notes an inconsistency in the whisker array arrangement (5x7 with zero padding). No finding addresses whisker array geometry or padding.

The ground truth points out missing hyperparameter adjustments for balancing two datasets with different physics fidelity. No finding mentions dataset construction or hyperparameter tuning for dataset imbalance.

The ground truth concerns selective reporting of only the best models rather than the full performance distribution. Finding 10 criticizes the claim of saturating explainable variance given limited stimuli, but does not identify the selective reporting issue.
The ground truth exaggerates the necessity of tactile augmentations and claims image augmentations caused training failure. No finding discusses augmentations or this rhetorical overgeneralization.
The ground truth identifies a downplayed ethical reflection on dataset limitations. No finding mentions ethical considerations or missing transparency about data constraints.
The ground truth questions the biological plausibility of the ±1 N force clipping relative to bite forces. No finding mentions force ranges or clipping.
The ground truth notes missing hyperparameter and hardware-scaling details for SSL vs. supervised training. No finding addresses this methodological omission.

The ground truth highlights zero decoding accuracies for several models, which are improbable. Finding 9 discusses a model performing exactly at chance (0.50), not the zero scores, and thus does not identify the same anomaly.
The ground truth describes missing equation definitions and skipped numbering in the Appendix. No finding mentions equations or reproducibility issues in the Appendices.

The ground truth is a cross-section inconsistency between the Abstract's strong alignment claim and the Discussion's acknowledgment of limited datasets. No finding identifies this specific cross-sectional contradiction.
The ground truth flags an overinterpreted speculation that GPT-based attenders indicate biological attention mechanisms. No finding addresses this speculative claim in the Discussion.
The ground truth points out failure to discuss biases from the small sample (11 mice, 999 units). No finding mentions sample size limitations or associated biases.
The ground truth concerns unfair comparison due to lack of balancing parameter counts or hyperparameter tuning across architectures. No finding discusses experimental fairness or parameter balancing.

Finding 4 reports an impossible maximum inter-animal correlation of 1.34 in Appendix A4, directly matching the ground truth that neural fit scores exceed plausible biological consistency and indicating calculation/reporting errors, even though the phrasing differs.
The ground truth describes a fabricated claim of being the first direct neural comparison and misattributed citations in Related Work. No finding mentions this novelty claim or reference errors.
